A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMAIA system. All nine pages of v2 and ten pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations, and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Tables I–II and Section IV.D report original map-query accuracy, venue-ranking results, and spatial-understanding accuracy, object counts, and inference times.

after.justification: Sections 4.1, 4.3, and 4.4 retain the original experiments. Section 4.2 additionally reports walking-time measurements across ten navigation scenarios.

M1.justification: The map-grounding pipeline, CLIP/XGBoost venue ranker, bearing-based navigation, and three-stage spatial-model distillation remain. Section 3.1.2 explicitly describes the existing grid as quadkey-indexed, but the PDFs do not establish an algorithmic replacement. Abbreviated training documentation likewise does not establish changed training.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 extends the illustrated navigation case to explicitly evaluated turn-required, non-visible destinations and visible destinations with possible temporary occlusion. This expands tested environmental conditions within the existing navigation task; map-query, venue-ranking, and street-view task coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the three map-query baselines, distance and similarity rankers, Florence-VL 8B, ASM v2, and the agent-based pipeline. Turn-by-turn navigation was already the comparator in v2's navigation section.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds a quantitative protocol using ten navigation scenarios, divided into four turn-required and six visible-destination cases, with average walking time and time relative to turn-by-turn navigation. The 4,300 map queries, 500/50 venue training/test queries, and 400-image spatial evaluation with the o1 judge remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The navigation section adds a condition-stratified analysis of guidance benefits for turn-required versus visible-destination scenarios. V2 provided an illustrative route comparison without these grouped measurements. No new component ablations or broader robustness studies appear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added navigation averages have no accompanying dispersion or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 newly reports walking times of 3.28 versus 2.08 minutes for turn-required cases and 3.36 versus 1.07 minutes for visible-destination cases, reported as 63.5% and 32.1% of turn-by-turn time. Tables I/1 and II/2 are numerically unchanged, as are spatial accuracy of 84% versus 27%, approximately seven versus four objects, and inference times of 1.7 versus 12.4 seconds.

T1.justification: The bearing, relative-direction, precision, and recall equations are unchanged. The quadkey discussion adds implementation terminology and explanation, without new formal definitions, mathematical reasoning, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central integrated-assistant and performance claims remain. V4 adds an explicit first-framework novelty claim and asserts modular, interchangeable vision-language backends that can be replaced without changing system behavior. These extend the claims about the retained system.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly interprets the results as supporting model-agnostic modularity and production-ready quality, beyond v2's emphasis on integrated grounding and practical accuracy and latency. No backend-replacement evaluation or substantive limitations discussion accompanies this broader interpretation.

D1.justification: V4 substantially reduces the spatial-model reproduction recipe: it omits five mining prompts per image, retention of the top ten entities, over fifteen query variants per image, and Florence-2-large with full-parameter training. Quadkey indexing is newly explicit, but the removed corpus-construction and training specifications materially reduce reproducibility. Their omission does not demonstrate changed settings.

R1.justification: V4 adds references on Bing map tiling, Set-of-Mark prompting, multimodal search, robustness, and distillation, while removing the Florence-2, GPT-4o system-card, and GPT-4o-mini references. The two related-work subsections remain substantively stable, although the introduction adds the first-integrated-framework claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial portions of the introduction, contribution bullets, spatial-understanding description, and conclusion are rewritten around three capabilities and last-100-meter use. The grid subsection is renamed and expanded, the distillation description is compressed, and heading conventions change throughout.

P2.justification: V4 extensively reformats the title, author block, abstract, headings, captions, tables, and page composition. It removes v2 Figure 1, redraws the workflow comparison as Figure 2, and redistributes retained illustrations. Most image content, including the grid illustration and navigation screenshots, is reused.

improvement.justification: The ten-scenario timing evaluation supplies useful quantitative support beyond v2's navigation illustration, and the revised framing clarifies the application. However, v4 removes important distillation specifications and asserts backend interchangeability without testing it. Stronger navigation evidence and clearer presentation coexist with weaker reproducibility and broader unvalidated claims, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
